result.reason: 3 findings, 2 of them important, and 2 dropped.

findings.label: F6
findings.problem: openTimeInMinutesOf() returns null when the day has no date (no start date). It also returns null when the stop's schedule times aren't known, for example when the leg isn't routed for the selected stops. No test checks either of these null results. The only null test covers a stop with no selected place, and one covers a place with no hours.
findings.failure_case: Delete the `date === null` check, or the `entry.startMinute === null || entry.endMinute === null` check. The next calls would read weekday on null or pass null minutes to openMinutesWithin. Every test in calendar-schedule.test.ts would still pass, because none asks for the open time on an itinerary with no start date or on an unrouted day.
findings.label_reason: The change adds these null results in a new function, and no test would fail if they were removed or wrong, so F6 fits. Nothing above F6 fits, because the code itself does the right thing.

findings.label: F6
findings.problem: scheduleTimeAt() leaves a time empty when it is two days or more after the day's midnight, since a ScheduleTime holds only the day's own date and the next one. No test reaches a minute of 2880 or more.
findings.failure_case: Remove `|| minute >= 2 * MINUTES_IN_DAY`. A stop ending at minute 2900 would show as 0:20 a.m., next day, which is a day too early. Every test would still pass, because the latest time any test reaches is about 2:15 a.m. the next day.
findings.label_reason: This cutoff is new behavior the change adds, and no test checks it, so F6 fits. The code is right as written, so the labels above F6 don't fit.

findings.label: NF1
findings.problem: #driveMinutesOf() works out `Math.ceil((minutes * (100 + percent)) / 100)` in floating point. With a fractional buffer percent, a result that should be a whole number can come out a hair above it. Math.ceil then rounds it up by a full minute.
findings.failure_case: With driveBufferPercent 28.8 and a 125-minute segment, the expression gives 161.00000000000003. The drive shows as 162 minutes instead of 161. A run over 1 to 600 minutes and buffer percents in steps of 0.1 found 12 such cases.
findings.label_reason: The result is wrong only for a fractional buffer percent such as 28.8, a setting no one would plausibly choose, so it isn't normal use and gets NF1 instead of F1. The change added this line, so it's a nit.

dropped.problem: The timeline decides a stop is selected by `visitTimeInMinutes !== null`, while #driveMinutesOf counts segments by `selectedPlace !== null`. A stop with a selected place and no visit time would shift every drive segment by one.
dropped.label: D1
dropped.reason: Stop enforces that the two always come together. Stop.#selectCandidate sets both. Clearing sets both to null. The visitTimeInMinutes setter refuses a value while selectedPlace is null. The constructor check (stop.ts lines 210-217) refuses a selected place with no visit time, and a visit time with no place.

dropped.problem: openMinutesWithin could miss or double-count an overlap for a visit that runs past the end of the week, such as a Saturday visit after midnight, or a period that wraps from Saturday into Sunday.
dropped.label: D1
dropped.reason: WEEKS_AROUND [-1, 0, 1, 2] covers every shift a visit of under two days can need. A period is at most one week long, since only a close at or before the open gets one week added. So at most one shift can overlap a given visit. The tests at open-minutes.test.ts lines 45-48 check both Saturday-to-Sunday cases (sunday 1-3 gives 60, saturday 23-27 gives 180). A hand check of a Saturday 23:00 to 27:00 visit against a Sunday 00:00 to 02:00 period gives 120.
